selected.selection_data: development only; no final-test metrics read

criteria.one_step_scale: frozen nominal delta scale; separate held-out query transitions
criteria.rollout_scale: fixed state scale; mean errors at steps 1..H

A.interpretation: Rollout-aware residual improves long horizons and preserves one-step adaptation

B.interpretation: Internal LoRA improves long horizons relative to output residual at a matched objective

C.interpretation: Both rollout objective and internal adaptation contribute

D.interpretation: Ridge consistently beats all neural methods at 100 steps

E.interpretation: Shift-specific effects require per-shift evidence, not an aggregate universal winner

F.interpretation: No material improvement of the tested factorial effects

questions.Q1: Rollout objective: residual median paired benefit 0.9%; positive in 58.5% of trials; 4/5 positive seed medians; LoRA median paired benefit 1.3%; positive in 60.4% of trials; 4/5 positive seed medians
questions.Q2: Internal location: one-step objective median paired benefit -20.5%; positive in 29.4% of trials; 0/5 positive seed medians; rollout objective median paired benefit -22.2%; positive in 29.6% of trials; 0/5 positive seed medians
questions.Q3: LoRA one-step adaptation: median paired benefit -30.4%; positive in 27.6% of trials; 0/5 positive seed medians
questions.Q4: One-step preserved within the predeclared 5% median tolerance: MetaResidual-1Step=True, MetaResidual-Rollout=True, MetaLoRA-1Step=False, MetaLoRA-Rollout=False
questions.Q5: Both-factor contribution plus one-step preservation criterion: False. Pairwise comparisons with all other adaptive methods are in combination_comparisons; no universal per-case winner is assumed.
questions.Q6: Consistent joint one-step/100-step Ridge winners: none
questions.Q7: See per_shift_metrics.csv and shift_effects in summary.json; signs vary by physical shift if outcome E is supported.
questions.Q8: Compare one-step preservation and the matched 100-step effects; these have distinct scales and are not directly subtracted.
questions.Q9: Endpoint error-growth ratios and comparable initial-error strata at 20 and 100 steps are saved in dynamics_growth_diagnostic_20 and dynamics_growth_diagnostic. A lower late-error/first-error ratio within the comparable initial-error band supports improved recursive behavior beyond a smaller initial error; it remains observational evidence, not proof of a causal dynamics mechanism.
questions.Q10: Each effect includes all five seed medians; material claims require at least four positive seed medians and no invalid/rejected paired outcomes.

one_step.definition: log(B1/B2) - log(A1/A2) at the same evaluation horizon
one_step.positive_interpretation: larger proportional rollout-objective effect for internal LoRA
one_step.interpretation: paired descriptive interaction; no significance or causal mechanism is claimed

rollout_100.definition: log(B1/B2) - log(A1/A2) at the same evaluation horizon
rollout_100.positive_interpretation: larger proportional rollout-objective effect for internal LoRA
rollout_100.interpretation: paired descriptive interaction; no significance or causal mechanism is claimed

dynamics_growth_diagnostic.metric: endpoint state-scale NMSE at H=100 divided by endpoint NMSE at H=1

physical_component_rmse_growth.definition: physical-unit RMSE averaged through H=100 divided by first-rollout-step RMSE
physical_component_rmse_growth.endpoint_vs_cumulative_distinction: This component diagnostic uses cumulative RMSE; endpoint NMSE above uses the endpoint only.

dynamics_growth_diagnostic_20.metric: endpoint state-scale NMSE at H=20 divided by endpoint NMSE at H=1

physical_component_rmse_growth.definition: physical-unit RMSE averaged through H=20 divided by first-rollout-step RMSE
physical_component_rmse_growth.endpoint_vs_cumulative_distinction: This component diagnostic uses cumulative RMSE; endpoint NMSE above uses the endpoint only.

recommended_adapter: Retain the V1 references; a new neural replacement is not justified
recommendation: Reconsider neural adaptation at CartPole complexity before adding more neural machinery or moving to Walker.
